rule.description: A merged workspace-resource capability contract aggregates abstract capability methods from two or more operation-family interfaces without implementing them, grafting all families onto every descendant; and any class below that merged interface whose inherited capability resolves to a body that performs no workspace request (no HTTP verb helper call on self, no self._client delegation), while some other subscriber of the same family serves it with a real request, is a forced, unused dependency of the fat interface.

checks.description: Detects a merged (fat) capability interface: a class that aggregates abstract capability methods from two or more operation-family interfaces without implementing them, grafting every family onto all descendant subscribers.
checks.detected_relation: merged contract class -> four unimplemented operation-family capability groups -> all descendant subscriber classes
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The umbrella contract makes every operation family a dependency of every workspace resource API, whether or not that resource can serve the family.

matches.evidence: WorkspaceResourceAPI merges the four capability groups (ResourceHealthAPI, ResourceRuntimeAPI, ResourceLifecycleAPI, ResourceModelCatalogAPI) into one fat interface and implements none of them, grafting all nine abstract capabilities (get_readiness, get_termination, get_replicas, get_log, get_events, stop, restart, list_supported_models, list_trainers) onto 13 descendant subscriber classes.

checks.description: Detects a class forced, only through the merged contract, to depend on capability families it cannot serve: each inherited obligation resolves to a body that performs no workspace request (no transport verb helper and no client delegation), while another subscriber of the same family serves it with a real request.
checks.detected_relation: resource API class -> merged contract -> inherited capability family it does not serve
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The subscriber's class surface claims support for operation families whose bodies only placate the inherited obligation, so every consumer of the resource type depends on capabilities the resource does not use.

matches.evidence: WorkloadResourceAPI resolves the model-catalog obligations (list_supported_models, list_trainers) inherited from the merged contract with empty-list placations and performs no workspace request, while the fine-tune API serves the same family with real requests.

ConfigurationResourceAPI resolves all nine merged obligations (get_readiness, get_termination, get_replicas, get_log, get_events, stop, restart, list_supported_models, list_trainers) with silent empty/no-op bodies and performs no workspace request, while the deployment and fine-tune APIs serve those families with real requests.

DeploymentAPI genuinely serves the health, runtime-visibility and lifecycle families with real routes, but through the merged contract it must also carry the fine-tune catalog obligations, placated with empty lists by the workload profile.

EndpointAPI genuinely serves the health, visibility and lifecycle families, but through the merged contract it must also carry the fine-tune catalog obligations, placated with empty lists by the workload profile.

DevPodAPI carries seven merged-contract obligations with no workspace request: its own get_readiness/get_termination/get_log refusals and empty replica/event placations, plus the profile-placated catalog obligations, while the deployment API serves those inspection and visibility families with real requests.

PodAPI carries empty replica/event placations and the profile-placated catalog obligations from the merged contract without any workspace request, while the deployment API serves the same families with real requests.

JobAPI carries the merged contract's health obligations as empty ReadinessIssue()/DeploymentTerminations() placations, its lifecycle obligations as canned refusals, and the profile-placated catalog obligations none of which perform a workspace request, while the deployment API genuinely serves health and lifecycle.

FineTuneAPI is the only genuine subscriber of the model-catalog family, yet must carry the merged contract's health, visibility and lifecycle obligations as empty views and canned refusals with no workspace request, while the deployment API serves those families with real requests.

SecretAPI, a pure configuration resource, is forced by the merged contract to depend on all nine capability families, resolved with silent empty/no-op bodies by the configuration profile while other resources serve them with real requests.

IngressAPI, a pure configuration resource, is forced by the merged contract to depend on all nine capability families, resolved with silent empty/no-op bodies by the configuration profile while other resources serve them with real requests.

TemplateAPI, a pure configuration resource, is forced by the merged contract to depend on all nine capability families, resolved with silent empty/no-op bodies by the configuration profile while other resources serve them with real requests.

RayClusterAPI, a pure configuration resource, is forced by the merged contract to depend on all nine capability families, resolved with silent empty/no-op bodies by the configuration profile while other resources serve them with real requests.

DedicatedNodeGroupAPI, a node-group management resource, is forced by the merged contract to depend on all nine capability families, resolved with silent empty/no-op bodies by the configuration profile while other resources serve them with real requests.

excluded.reason: A log-query service rather than a workspace lifecycle resource; not subscribed to the merged contract and not part of the credited relation.
A hardware-resource catalog reader with no lifecycle surface; outside the merged contract.

excluded.target: Basic data verbs (list_all/get/create/update/delete) on every resource API
excluded.reason: Per-resource data operations with deliberately resource-specific shapes; not capability-family obligations of the merged contract.

excluded.target: Pre-existing deliberate degradation bodies that route through the workspace client
excluded.reason: Bodies that delegate via self._client (or issue transport calls) count as genuine service under this rule; only bodies with no workspace interaction at all are credited.

excluded.target: Abstract capability declarations in the per-family contracts themselves
excluded.reason: These are the grafting material of the merged interface, not classes below it; only the merging class and its descendants are credited matches.
